
== Japanese original printing source audit ==
Original Japanese source: encyclopedia p. 41, embedded JPEG xref 2036. <ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 41, 99. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Image SHA256 <code style="white-space:normal;overflow-wrap:anywhere">a340f126a66cc54684f599732a963d827bbe2066137d5865265b46e596364ed0</code>. The original image is [[:File:Japanese-Premiere-Millennium-Falcon-Encyclopedia32-original.jpg]]. Printed wraps joined; ASCII digits, Latin letters, +, =, < and > normalized. Unique asterisk tracked separately; Tarkin lore underline retained. Original JPEG remains typography authority. The Japanese lore describes [[Lando Calrissian]] losing the sabacc bet and handing the ship to [[Han Solo]], while the original English describes ownership until Han won it. The Japanese calls the docking capability ドッキング能力, while the English says "ship-docking capability." Both printed game texts require a pilot to use power, maneuver or hyperspeed; neither assigns zero to those printed statistics when unpiloted. Printed absence is separate from rule-derived defaults and unknown data. No artist/translator credit is visible. Performer likeness attribution and Japanese GEMP implementation remain unresolved. The November 1998 tournament-language rule is dated context, not evidence of earlier or custom-format mechanics. No new rules or implementation equivalence is claimed.
